slides.0.title: Geography and climate
slides.0.subtitle: The long, narrow land, the Andes and Coastal Range, the Humboldt Current and irrigation
slides.1.title: A long, narrow country
slides.1.highlights.0.title: It starts in desert
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The Atacama Desert in the north gets under 10 mm of rain a year, so vineyards depend on irrigation
slides.1.highlights.1.title: 14 main DO valleys
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth describes the country as about 14 main DO valleys (its list actually has 16 names, so the number is only a guide), stretching across a large range of latitude
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Latitude and terroir
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Within one country the north is hot and dry and the south cool and wet; Level 2 goes region by region
slides.1.content: Chile is a long, thin wine country, and latitude alone brings varied terroirs.
slides.2.title: The cold current, the Coastal Range and the Andes
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The Humboldt Current
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The cold current runs north along the coast, bringing morning fog and afternoon sea breezes to the coastal zones
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The Coastal Cordillera
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Rising to roughly 700–2,500 m (Wine With Seth), it partly blocks maritime influence from reaching the interior
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The Andes
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Aconcagua rises to 6,961 m; snowmelt is the main water source
slides.2.content: A cold current and Coastal Range in the west and the Andes in the east cut Chile into west-to-east terroir bands.
slides.3.title: Irrigation and phylloxera
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Snowmelt irrigation
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Vineyards use Andean snowmelt, delivered through canals and modern drip systems
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Phylloxera has not established
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth notes phylloxera never established in Chile, leaving a large reservoir of ungrafted vinifera (in contrast to Europe)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Going further
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The current state of own-rooted vines is covered in Level 3 and checked against official data
slides.3.content: Chile is a snowmelt-irrigated wine country without phylloxera pressure.
Annual rainfall in the Atacama Desert is below roughly what?
What does the Humboldt Current bring to the coast?
A. Morning fog and afternoon sea breezes
The cold current brings fog and sea breezes.
What is the main water source for Chilean vineyards?
